# The murex pack

*Murex* · version 1.0.0 · code `MURX`

## What it is

Murex is the cross-asset trading and risk platform. Its trades arrive in the common UPPER_SNAKE trade schema, so the mapping is the identity.
This pack is one source of the canonical `trade` kind: its rows carry `SOURCE_SYSTEM = MUREX`. It is a pack of the `trading-systems` module that
extends `trading`; switch it on or off in Admin -> Artifacts (the pack is the switch).

## Data structures

Every kind the pack owns, read from its manifest, its samples and its Sutras: how its ids look, its fields (type, an example, what it means), its nested lists and the fields that link to other kinds. A path `A[].B` is field `B` of every element of list `A`.

## Enabling and dependencies

Builds on the packs `trading`.

The connectors it brings (written once to `config/connectors/<name>.yaml`, then the site's own):

| Connector | Plugin | Kinds | Enabled |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trade-murex` | `delta` | `trade` | `${DRISHTI_LAKE_ENABLED:true}` |
| `trade-murex-live` | `kafka` | `trade` | `${DRISHTI_STREAM_MUREX:false}` |

Settings (environment variables) its connectors read: `DRISHTI_LAKE_ENABLED`, `DRISHTI_MUREX_TOPIC`, `DRISHTI_STREAM_MUREX`, `DRISHTI_STREAM_STALE_AFTER`.

## Refreshing the data

The pack's files are written by `tools/packgen/readme.py murex`; its `--check` fails when the committed files differ from what it would write.
